column8: Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: twin of Q13-019 (fix the analysis before the outcome can be seen); adds only ICH E9's duty to report an unplanned look, and medicine never enters the report (Q29-016); its date is wrong: Caplet submitted the IPS on 6 Nov, before the Sat 7 Nov 09:00 Sydney deadline.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 and 3e store: watching whether the plan is carried out (notices, trade days) is a different job from watching how it does, which is why the middle level changes a date or an instrument, never the plan (D19); medicine stays out, one plain clause at most.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e and Table 3 rows 1-2, the card's aha as one plain clause: Laura sees prices daily, so both reasons are read without a price; fix: say neither reason is a market price (D20, professor 19: a missed deposit can be her choice), never 'no price can pull either trigger', and date it from January 2028; carries row 25.

Mon 23 Nov: 3d store: a figure moved after a market move reads as the market's figure, not hers; the case's credibility warning already carries it, and Laura restates only after a default (Table 3 row 2), never after a price move.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: twin of Q15-001 (a trigger prompts a look, never an automatic act) and Q29-005; keep its guard: never say a missed deposit forces a change (Table 3 row 1 says what it changes and never changes).

Mon 23 Nov: 3e and Table 3, one plain clause: both reasons are money that fails to arrive, and IPS l.17's 'only' shuts a rise out as firmly as a fall, so a rise changes the top she may state, never a step of the plan; the FDA source stays out of the report.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: the outside basis for keeping two lists (Q109-033, Q137-041): a closed list of reasons is honest only beside the open list of ways each promise breaks; never 'only two things can break the plan'; FDA is never cited in the report.

Mon 23 Nov: Section 2 (2.3) and Table 3 row 1 store: a smaller deposit is absorbed by the order of purchase without reading a price (aha 2, NUMBERS 8u); a missed one breaks no stated figure, it delays the range; never a rule for a smaller deposit (A34, D9).
Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: the default's meaning, hold and wait (Table 3 row 2, Never: a forced sale), already in the tree's branch 6; FDA's 2024 text is a draft not in effect, store only.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e and Section 2 store: twin of H9-093 (Guide p.5: planned adjustments yes, redesign after results no, the 2031 move a planned step); adds only FDA's prespecified-adaptation wording, which stays out.
Mon 23 Nov: 3c store: twin of row 19 (an early reading overstates); judges' reasoning behind aha 7 only, whose own figure (about 11 of 100) is what the report says.
Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: what acting at every look costs, in the field that measured it; Armitage not read at source; never carried to Laura as a number (no NUMBERS figure) and never in the report.
Mon 23 Nov: Store only: the price of looking set before looking; the rule exists to allow an early stop and the plan has none on prices, so it serves no part beyond row 14's limit case.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 row 6 store: the limit case of a very high bar (any level, none); true only for the plan's steps and stated figures, since prices still move the top before 2031; Haybittle and Peto read only second-hand.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 row 5 store: the timing flexes, the deadline and the order do not (never past the 2031 meetings; never the step or its order); medicine stays out.

Mon 23 Nov: 3c and 3e, the lead's reasoning for claim 1: what protects a stated figure is its date (she states the top once it is held, D1), not l.17's sentence; abstract only and disputed (row 17, the July 2010 letters), so never a figure in the report.

Mon 23 Nov: 3c store: the counterweight to row 16, early looks cost most; mapping share prices onto a trial's information fraction is loose, so it supports only the move's date (NUMBERS 8r), never a figure.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: the reason for a change is the first thing lost, which Table 3's last column already prevents by writing each response down first; about reporting, not decisions.

Mon 23 Nov: 3c store, judges' reasoning behind aha 7 (a figure read off a random high is one the later reading will not support); the report keeps aha 7's own number, never this sentence; carries row 11.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e and Table 3 rows 1-2, one plain clause: both reasons are an input that fails to arrive or an instrument that fails, never a reading of how the plan is doing, which is why a market fall is not one; the vaccine trial stays out.

Mon 23 Nov: Section 2 store: twin of Q29-008 (changes reported with reasons); Table 1's note keeps D3's words only (never 'we changed', 'after the freeze' or 'a new standard'), so a reporting standard is no frame for it.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of Q7b-036 (an outside standard whose parts Table 3 already holds: named events, a named watcher, what each changes and never changes); adds SPIRIT's who-decides item; never invent a decider (A34).
Mon 23 Nov: 3e store, claim 1's hard test: written rules get rewritten, and naming in advance only makes a rewrite detectable by whoever checks the record; research reporting, never in the report.
Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: a rule works where someone checks the outcome against the record; for Caplet the record is the submitted IPS and the checkers the judges; supports row 31, never in the report.
Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: twin of row 3 (deciders who see results along the way react to them); medicine's answer is secrecy, the plan's that from January 2028 no promised dollar waits on a reaction.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 row 2 store: a named harm, a set number and a stated response, the shape row 2 already has; nothing medical in the report.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 and 3e store: one stated handling per foreseeable event; treating market moves as irrelevant to the promises is the treatment-policy idea, true by the deletion test; too technical to say plainly, so the lead's reasoning only.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e store, the comparison's main break: a trial needs early exits because waiting harms patients, while the promised money loses nothing by waiting; say it needs no exit on prices, and keep the limit that waiting in a fall can cost her flexibility before 2031.

Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: twin of Q109-032 (no price is in any failure set, the deletion test) and Q165 idea 1 (the Treasuries bind, the sentence does not); adds only that the trial lens fits the top before the move.
Mon 23 Nov: 3e store: twin of row 31 (the plan's outside readers are the judges and, from 2031, co-sponsors who see the fund's statement); never propose a monitor or a new check (A34).

Mon 23 Nov: 3e, the lead's reasoning on why l.17's last sentence holds: not because it was written down but because nothing promised waits on a market reading; fix: date it from January 2028, since before the deposit the ten wait on it (D20); close to Q165 idea 1, so one cold reader before any use.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store, the scale: a watch fails from firings that ask nothing, not from rows; fix the count: Table 3 has six dated cells, but row 2 is read on each coupon date of the five bonds (15 Feb, May, Aug, Nov), so about 30 looks in 2027-2032, still far below any limit; carries row 12.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: what a noisy watch costs; it serves claim 2, which the card kills (Laura's risk is too little to watch), so background only.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a watch list's cost never reaches zero; background only, no part needs it.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 13 (a wider limit trades false alarms for late catches) and row 31 (levels by speed of response); adds nothing row 2 or the level headings lack.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of Q30-002 (a row earns its place if missing it alone breaks a promise); the hospital version adds nothing to the killer-item test.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of Q7b-036 (an outside standard whose parts Table 3 already holds); the map is loose (Never: is not when parameters can be changed), so never 'meets a hospital standard', and nothing medical in the report.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: why the Carry on while column earns its width: saying in advance when a reading needs nothing keeps the other firings believed; method, never named.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a quiet row is not a dead row, so the default row stays though it may never fire (Q30-002's killer item); its disanalogy (hospital alarms grew with devices) is recorded.
Mon 23 Nov: Store only: feeling managed outruns having a process; a self-selected survey, and card Q221 holds the named watcher.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: fatigue limits are orders of magnitude away; fix the Keel count: besides the six dated cells, row 2 is read on each coupon date (four a year from the five bonds), so say about 30 dated looks in 2027-2032, never about six.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 18 (the signal was there, attention was the gap); the ICU figures add nothing Table 3's dates need.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 1 (most alarms need nothing); its map is wrong: the level whose firings need nothing is Watch (rows 6-7), while the middle level changes a date or an instrument.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 row 2 store: the five-business-day threshold is set wide so a one-day delay is never called a default (Q30-029); fix 'never falsely' to 'late rather than falsely', since 1979's late payments, back to normal in under three weeks (Q30-027), would have crossed it; carries row 4.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a measured number for too many empty firings (tens in two hours); Table 3 never nears it, so length is not what binds; carries row 26.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 16 (a standing watch decays, a prompt restores it); a lab of hours, not years, and Mackworth read only in the APA record.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 and 3e wording guard: never 'monitor closely' or 'stay alert' in the table or 3e; a dated occasion (a trade day, 31 March 2028) is what works; carries row 15.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 row 2 store: the rarest row is where a first late payment is likeliest waved off as a glitch, so its trigger is a count of days, not a judgment, as built.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3, the reason each plan-changing row has an occasion to be read (a dated deadline, a counted delay): the commonest failure is not looking; abstract only; carries rows 11 and 19.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 18 (information present and not attended to); same author, same use.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a reading means something only against a threshold, which is why each firing row sets Carry on while beside Look closer or act when; row 6 rightly has none.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: the table is an external memory cue whose levels sort what may be dropped before any pressure arrives; Laura is rarely under load, so method only.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: levels of 2, 3 and 2 each fit one glance, and the two reasons are one chunk she can carry without the table; textbook, background only.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 writers' guard: one page shows what is happening, never why; the why stays in 3e's prose and notes, never back in the cells (the Tue 17 Nov cut).
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: Table 3 is a calendar of looks, not a live dashboard, so its dates matter more than its layout; a disanalogy that sharpens the form.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a firing whose answer is decided in advance (row 5, wait day by day) belongs below the top level, and only rows 1-2 ask for judgment; close to Q30-014, adds only the robotic-response test.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 14 (a numbered limit for too many urgent firings, far above Table 3's).

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 rows 1-3 and 3e, one clause of method: rows 1-2 fire on symptoms (no deposit received, a payment late), while a career slump and a debt-limit standoff are causes watched only through them, because the cause cries wolf (all 13 standoffs of 2011-2025 ended with no missed payment, Q15-024); Google never named.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 Who column store: one reader a row (Laura for rows 1 and 7, the team for the rest), never both, so no row is left to the other; card Q221 holds the named watcher.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3's three levels, a basis-column note at most: act, look closer and watch match Google's pages, tickets and logging, and a table nobody is told to read on a date is the inbox it warns against; never a parallel in 3e.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 and one clause of 3e method: the danger for a table read about 30 times in six years is too few firings, so when row 1 or 2 fires each Changes cell already spells out the act; no drill proposed (A34).

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3's levels, a basis-column note at most: certified airliners sort alerts into three levels by what a firing asks, and the strongest mark (the first level's heading) stays with rows 1-2 only; carries row 32.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: twin of row 31 (keep the strongest mark for the most severe events); ISA 18.2 read only as the FAA handbook quotes it.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 rows 2-3 and 3e store: a trigger that forecasts a rare default would almost always be false, so row 2 waits for the payment and row 3 changes nothing before the deadline; beside Q15-024; quote 1 in 59 as the paper's (its stated rates give about 1 in 60).
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: people answer an alarm as often as it has been true, so rows 1-2, which fire only on the event, earn a full answer; a lab of 138 students.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: false firings are survivable when the reader knows in advance what they mean, which the Never: half of each cell says; experts on a busy scope, method only.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: three levels with a cautious top level, never a fourth; the two studies conflict on how much three stages add.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a short list works when each item is an act aimed at one failure (Q30-014's rule); Gawande read only in excerpts; background.
Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 store: a list ticked is not a list acted on, the counterweight to Q13-022's checklist gain; Table 3 already names an act and a person in each row, so nothing changes.

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3 row 7: true that it has no date to look, but row 7 never changes the range, so it stays a watch as built; no reading date at the 2031 meetings or anywhere (update 3, CANON A34; its building-cost trigger was declined Sat 14 Nov).

Mon 23 Nov: Table 3, the 27 Nov evidence for leaving its length and form alone and refusing a debt-limit or market-level trigger; fix: drop 'except one (row 7's date)', since row 7 is a watch without a date by design (A34).
